walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical Chemistry — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physical Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physical Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Members of a homologous series share:
options: The same molecular mass
The same functional group and general formula
The same boiling point
The same number of isomers

mcqs.q: Can you determine the order of a reaction with respect to a reactant from the balanced equation?
options: The order of reaction is always equal to the number of reactants in the equation.
No — orders must be determined experimentally; they often differ from the stoichiometric coefficients.
The standard hydrogen electrode has a potential of -1 V to balance copper at +1 V.
The order of reaction with respect to each reactant equals its coefficient in the balanced equation.

mcqs.q: In a standard hydrogen electrode used as a reference, what is the assigned electrode potential?
options: The salt bridge prevents the solutions from reacting with each other.
The standard hydrogen electrode actually has zero potential because hydrogen has no charge.
Exactly 0 V by convention — all other electrode potentials are measured relative to it.
The standard hydrogen electrode has a potential of -1 V to balance copper at +1 V.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a salt bridge in an electrochemical cell?
options: The salt bridge carries electrons between the two electrodes.
The salt bridge prevents the solutions from reacting with each other.
It completes the circuit by allowing ions to flow between the half-cells, maintaining electrical neutrality.
The standard hydrogen electrode has a potential of -1 V to balance copper at +1 V.
